description: UNOS feature ledger (ADR-0203): the user-visible features and the planned changes, each with the steps that verify it. passes turns true only after every step passed as a user scenario: the tests in verified_by assert each step, the E2E specs on the local stand-in cover the steps in the web UI, and an entry whose steps make a host-level change (GLOSSARY.md) has also passed a device check and a re-check after a reboot of the deployed tree (ADR-0018). A pass also needs a reviewer in a fresh context who tried to refute the change, with each finding fixed or recorded (ADR-0017). A failing re-check, or a step that its tests do not assert as written, sets passes back to false. A pass changes only passes, verified_by and notes; changing a description or the steps, or dropping an entry, needs a new ADR that names the entry's id, and a changed entry lists that ADR in adr. supervisor/tests/test_feature_list.py compares the ledger with the one at the branch's merge base with main, where an ADR is new when its number is not in that base's docs/adr, and skips the comparison while that base has no ledger: until the ledger is merged into main neither a local run nor CI catches a dropped or reworded entry (ci.ledger-changes-checked). The feature-pass skill carries one entry per pass.

features.description: Issues on GitHub are triaged with the labels needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human and wontfix
steps: The GitHub repository has the five labels, and bug and enhancement
An issue opened from the bug or the enhancement template gets needs-triage
An accepted issue gets ready-for-agent or ready-for-human and a feature-list.json entry; a rejected one gets wontfix with the reason in the issue
features.notes: Owner action: the labels are made in the owner's GitHub account.

features.description: Branches merged into main are deleted, on GitHub and in local worktrees
steps: git branch -r --merged origin/main lists only origin/main
GitHub deletes the head branch of a merged pull request by itself
git worktree list shows no worktree of a merged branch
features.notes: Owner action on GitHub: 20 merged remote branches remain (19 claude/* and phase0-hardening). On 2026-11-07 the 21 branches merged into main were deleted on GitHub by hand; nothing deletes them automatically yet.

features.description: The network, power, time zone, hostname, firewall, log, NFS and SMART actions read and change the host through src/host.py
steps: Setting the time zone or the hostname changes them on the host: timedatectl and hostnamectl on the host show the new values
Reboot, shutdown and their cancel act on the host
Firewall rules are the host's ufw rules, and NFS exports are the host's /etc/exports
Logs come from the host's journal, and SMART data from the host's smartctl
A test fails when one of these routers runs a host command without host.run_on_host
features.notes: Today several of these commands run inside the supervisor container, or call nsenter themselves. Shared preparation for system.power, system.hostname-and-time-zone, system.logs-viewer, security.host-firewall and shares.nfs-exports.

features.description: Every data path of the supervisor follows one setting, UNOS_DATA_DIR, so the backend runs outside its container without patched module constants
steps: UNOS_DATA_DIR=<dir> starts the supervisor with its database, secrets, state files, certificates and backups under <dir>
Host paths such as /etc/fstab and /run/samba keep settings of their own
scripts/standin/run_supervisor.py sets UNOS_DATA_DIR and patches no module constant
tests/test_standin.py finds no hard-coded /data path in supervisor/src
features.notes: About 15 module-level /data paths are hard-coded today; the stand-in redirects them one by one. The health handlers in supervisor/src/main.py read /data/unos.db, /data/raid_status.json and /data/ups_config.json directly: the READ_ONLY_PROBES of tests/test_standin.py.

features.description: Changes to existing database tables ship as Alembic migrations
steps: alembic upgrade head on an empty database creates the whole schema
A change to an existing table comes with a revision, and the supervisor applies pending revisions at startup
A test runs every revision on a database made by the one before
features.notes: Today create_all only adds new tables (ADR-0077). Decide ADR-0022 before the first change to an existing table; without other installations (ADR-0207) the dev device's database may be reset instead.

features.description: The supervisor logs structured lines with level, logger and fields, and handlers log the exceptions they catch
steps: Every log line of the supervisor is one JSON object with time, level, logger and message
A handler that catches an exception logs it with its traceback before it answers
supervisor/src has no print() calls

features.description: JSON state files are replaced atomically, and a file that cannot be parsed is kept and reported instead of reset
steps: A supervisor killed while it writes a state file leaves the old or the new content, never a partial file
A state file that cannot be parsed is renamed to <name>.bad and named in a warning, and the defaults are used

features.description: Every time the API stores or returns carries its time zone
steps: Timestamps in API answers are ISO 8601 with an offset
The database stores times in UTC
The web UI shows times in the browser's time zone

features.description: The supervisor's OpenAPI schema describes every endpoint, its fields and its errors, with examples
steps: Every route of app.openapi() has a summary and a description
Every field of the request and response models has a description, and the models have examples
Each route lists the error statuses it answers

features.description: Extensions add storage backends, notification channels or sign-in providers without changes to UNOS itself
steps: A storage backend (for example ZFS or mdadm) can be added as a plugin, and one exists
A notification channel can be added as a plugin
A sign-in provider (for example LDAP or OAuth) can be added as a plugin
features.notes: Needs an ADR on whether UNOS takes plugins at all.

features.description: Two UNOS hosts share one configuration, and one takes over the services when the other fails
steps: Two hosts run UNOS against one shared configuration
Stopping one host moves its shares and apps to the other within a stated time
features.notes: Needs an ADR first; out of scope while UNOS has one dev device.

features.description: The web UI is served only over HTTPS with certificates from Caddy's local CA and with security headers; plain HTTP redirects
steps: https://<host>/ loads with Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
API answers carry the same headers
http://<host>/<path> redirects to https://<host>/<path>
GET /api/v1/health still answers over plain HTTP
features.notes: The stand-in serves these headers through scripts/standin/front.mjs. Device check: 2026-11-05 (Phase 0 deploy, also after a reboot of that tree); the deployed tree changed since. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC), from the device: https://127.0.0.1/ and /api/v1/health answer with Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, http://127.0.0.1/storage answers 308 to https://127.0.0.1/storage, and /api/v1/health answers 200 over plain HTTP.

features.description: Request bodies, WebSocket messages and login fields are limited before the credentials are checked
steps: An anonymous POST with a 2 MiB JSON body answers 413, and the body is not read
A signed-in 2 MiB JSON body answers 413, also when it is sent chunked
A WebSocket message over 64 KiB closes the socket
A login with a field over its limit answers 422, and audit entries store bounded fields only
File and backup uploads stream past 1 MiB under their own limits
features.notes: The limit is a middleware in front of every route (supervisor/src/request_limits.py); not host-level. Step 1: test_request_limits.py (test_content_length_over_the_limit_is_answered_413_without_reading, also for the login, test_content_length_over_the_limit_is_answered_before_anything_is_received, test_chunked_body_over_the_limit_gets_413, test_chunked_body_is_counted_and_reading_stops_at_the_limit, and test_a_real_server_answers_413_for_chunked_and_declared_bodies with both of uvicorn's HTTP parsers). Step 2: test_a_signed_in_client_gets_413_for_a_declared_and_a_chunked_body (a valid administrator token, GET /auth/me answers 200, then a declared and a chunked 2 MiB body each answer 413); the note that said it was missing was stale: note and test came in the same commit (2e4306d, 2026-11-07). Step 3: test_uvicorn_refuses_a_large_first_message_before_the_application_gets_it and test_both_images_limit_websocket_messages_alike (uvicorn's --ws-max-size in both images). Step 4: test_login_bounds.py. Step 5: test_request_limits.py (each upload's own limit) and test_upload_streaming.py (the uploads stream into their destination, and the server's memory does not grow); its tests of unnamed files run on Linux only (scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh) and concern files.upload, not the limits. Passed 2026-11-09.

features.description: Sign-ins and administrative actions are recorded in the audit log, which an administrator lists, filters and exports
steps: Sign in, create a user and delete it: GET /api/v1/audit/logs lists the three entries with user, action, time and client address
Filters by user, action and time narrow the list, and GET /api/v1/audit/logs/count counts it
GET /api/v1/audit/logs/export downloads the filtered entries
features.notes: Step 1: TestSignInAndUserManagementAreListed in tests/test_audit_log.py signs in, creates and deletes a user through the API and reads the three entries from GET /api/v1/audit/logs, newest first, with the user, the action, the time and the client address. Step 2: TestFilters and TestSearch filter by user, action, severity, time and text, at the edges of a day and of a second, on entries with microseconds as log_action writes them, and /logs/count counts the same entries; a bound covers the whole day, hour, minute, second or fraction it names, and one in another form or with a zone gets 422 (ADR-0237). Step 3: TestExport downloads the filtered entries as CSV and JSON, the same entries the list shows, and in the CSV a ' keeps a spreadsheet from reading a value as a formula, the user name of a failed sign-in included. Recorded today: sign-ins, users and their SMB access, shares, API tokens, recovery codes and the clearing of the log (docs/USER_GUIDE.md, Audit Log); storage, snapshots, containers, apps, backups, power, scheduled tasks, the network, system settings and a user's own password and two-factor changes write no entries yet (security.audit-admin-actions). Writing entries is tested in tests/test_login_bounds.py and tests/test_audit_log.py, the administrator-only routes in tests/test_authz.py. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no device check needed. The page is webui.audit-log-page.

features.description: Every administrative action and every change of a user's own sign-in is recorded in the audit log, not only sign-ins, users, shares and API tokens
steps: Creating and deleting pools and volumes, and creating, deleting and restoring snapshots, write audit entries with the user, the client address and the resource
Starting, stopping and removing containers, and installing and uninstalling apps, write audit entries
Creating, restoring and deleting backups, restarting and shutting down, and changing scheduled tasks, the network and the system settings write audit entries
A user's own password change and turning two-factor authentication on or off write audit entries
Every AuditAction value that the Action filter of the Audit Log page offers is written by the action it names, or is removed
features.notes: A side finding of security.audit-log (ADR-0203): only the auth, shares and audit code call log_action (supervisor/src/audit/router.py), so POOL_*, VOLUME_*, SNAPSHOT_*, CONTAINER_*, APP_*, BACKUP_*, SYSTEM_*, SETTINGS_CHANGED, TASK_*, FIREWALL_*, SSL_CERT_UPLOADED, NETWORK_CONFIG_CHANGED, PASSWORD_CHANGE, TOTP_* and LOGOUT are never written. Entries record real changes only (ADR-0157).

features.description: Audit entries are appended to the log one line each, off the event loop and with rotation, instead of rewriting the whole file
steps: Sign in 100 times: the audit log grows by 100 lines, and the bytes written before stay as they were
An entry is written in a worker thread, never on the event loop
A damaged line is skipped, and the other entries are still listed
The log rotates at its size limit and keeps a fixed number of old files, which GET /api/v1/audit/logs still reads

On the dev device, sign-ins append one line each to /data/audit/audit.jsonl without rewriting it (its inode and earlier bytes stay), and the SD writes of a sign-in are measured before and after the deploy (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Device check on 2026-11-07 after the deploy: three sign-ins appended three lines of about 270 bytes, the file kept its inode and its earlier bytes, and GET /api/v1/audit/logs/count counted them. A sign-in wrote 0.156 to 0.168 MiB to the SD card, 0.172 to 0.195 MiB before with a small old log; the rest is the login history's SQLite commit (architecture.sqlite-write-cost). Step 5 was reworded by ADR-0224. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md): no reboot check needed. The old /data/audit_log.json was deleted on the device.

features.description: Each audit entry carries the hash of the one before, so an edited or removed entry is detected
steps: Every entry stores a hash over its content and the previous entry's hash
After an entry in the file is edited or deleted, GET /api/v1/audit/logs reports where the chain breaks
The chain continues across rotated files
features.notes: Builds on security.append-only-audit-log.

features.description: The supervisor bounds the size of request headers and the number of open connections
steps: The upload throughput over 2.5 GbE is measured with the HTTP parser and limits chosen, and stays at today's level
A request whose header block is over the limit is refused
Connections over the limit are refused while the open ones keep working

features.description: An administrator turns the host's UFW firewall on or off and adds and removes rules in System > Security
steps: Turn the firewall on in System > Security: ufw status on the host says active
Add a rule that allows a port from the LAN: the host's ufw lists it, and Delete removes it
The web UI, SSH and SMB stay reachable from the LAN with the firewall on
features.notes: The ufw commands run inside the supervisor container, not on the host (architecture.host-command-layer). The E2E spec only opens the section. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator uploads a certificate or makes a self-signed one in System > Security, and the web UI is served with it
steps: Upload a certificate with its key and chain: it is listed with its names and expiry date
Browsers then get that certificate from https://<host>/
Deleting it returns the web UI to the certificate of Caddy's local CA
features.notes: Stored certificates are listed, but Caddy serves only its local CA: nothing hands them to the web UI container.

features.description: The certificate code keeps no special cases for files that older versions wrote
steps: The fix-ups for private keys that older versions left 0644 and for certificate names they stored without validation are gone from supervisor/src/security/router.py
Every stored certificate and key goes through the one current path: validated, and keys written 0600
tests/test_security.py passes without tests of the old cases

features.description: On a new installation the first visit creates the one administrator, and setup is refused afterwards
steps: Open the web UI of a new installation: /setup asks for the administrator's name and password
Create the account: the dashboard opens, signed in as that administrator
A second setup, also one sent at the same moment as the first, answers 400 and creates nobody
No default account exists before setup
features.notes: webui/tests/first-run.spec.ts runs on the stand-in's real supervisor, on the new installation that scripts/standin/e2e.sh starts without any account: e2e.sh runs it alone with E2E_FIRST_RUN=1, never retried, before the specs, and stops when it fails (ADR-0261; test_standin.py checks that and that e2e.sh sends no setup request, and runs a copy of e2e.sh with a faked stand-in and Playwright: the setup with E2E_FIRST_RUN=1, then the specs without it, a stop when the setup fails). Named alone, scripts/standin/e2e.sh tests/first-run.spec.ts runs that setup as the whole run. Step 4: /api/v1/auth/status answers setup_required and admin/admin does not sign in. Step 1: the web UI leads to /setup, whose name and password fields are reached through their labels. Step 2: creating E2E_ADMIN there opens the dashboard with that name and Administrator in the sidebar. Step 3: a second setup through the page shows "Admin user already exists. Use /login instead.", and the users list holds only the first administrator. test_auth.py's TestFirstRunSetup adds two setups sent at the same moment (200 and 400, one administrator), a refused setup that creates nobody, the new administrator signing in, an app started on a new database without any account, and the one uvicorn process that _setup_lock needs. Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md). The compose test stack still creates its administrator through the API.

features.description: A user signs in with name and password and signs out
steps: Open the web UI without a session: the sign-in page is shown
Wrong credentials show an error, and no session starts
Right credentials open the dashboard
Sign out: the sign-in page is shown, and the session's token is gone from the browser
features.notes: Step 4: auth.spec.ts 'Logout ends the session' clicks Logout and checks that the token is gone (added on 2026-11-07, after a review found the step unasserted).

features.description: A user turns on TOTP two-factor authentication and then signs in with codes that work only once
steps: On the Account page, start the two-factor setup: the QR code is drawn in the browser
Enter a code from the authenticator app: two-factor authentication is on
Sign in: after the password the code form appears, and a valid code opens the dashboard
The same code a second time is refused, and the form says to wait for the next one
Turn two-factor authentication off with a code
features.notes: webui/tests/two-factor.spec.ts on the stand-in's real supervisor, for a regular test user (never E2E_ADMIN), with codes computed from the secret of the QR code (tests/totp.ts, RFC 6238). Step 1: Enable draws the QR code from a data: URL in the browser, and the image is, module by module, the QR code of the setup's otpauth://totp/UNOS:<name> URI (the qrcode package, error correction M), whose secret is the one shown for manual entry, with the issuer UNOS and SHA-1, 6 digits and 30 seconds. Step 2: a code turns 2FA on; the card says Enabled and /auth/totp/status agrees. Step 3: after the password the code form appears, and a code of the next 30-second step opens the dashboard. Step 4: the same code again, in the same step, answers "This two-factor code was already used; wait for the next one" and the code form stays. Step 5: a code of a newer step turns 2FA off, and the password alone signs in again. The spec waits for new steps (about 40 to 60 seconds). test_totp_once.py reads that URI as an app does (its secret is the stored one, and its code turns 2FA on) and covers the single use at every check, roles.spec.ts that no QR code service is asked, auth.spec.ts the errors of the code form. A status that cannot be loaded is reported with its reason and Retry, not shown as Disabled with Enable (security.spec.ts). Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md). A lost authenticator needs a recovery code (auth.recovery-codes); no administrator can reset another user's 2FA (system.emergency-runbook-and-cli).

features.description: Sign-in attempts are limited to 5 per minute per client
steps: Five failed sign-ins from one client answer 401, the sixth 429
Another client can still sign in meanwhile
The sign-in page shows the 429 message
features.notes: Not host-level. Steps 1 and 2: test_authz.py, test_login_rate_limit_is_per_client_not_global (five wrong passwords from one client answer 401, the sixth 429; another client behind the same proxy signs in with the right password, 200, while the first one still gets 429 with it, which a lockout of the account would not allow) and test_direct_connections_cannot_choose_their_address (a new X-Forwarded-For per attempt is no new bucket); the note that said step 2 was asserted only as a 401 was stale: note and the strengthened test came in the same commit (2e4306d, 2026-11-07). Step 3: auth.spec.ts on the stand-in, 'a sign-in refused for too many attempts says so and keeps the form' (added 2026-11-09: the 429 at the password step, which failed with the message taken out of webui/src/lib/api/client.ts) and 'errors in the 2FA step keep the code form unless the password was rejected' (the 429 at the code step). Passed 2026-11-09.

features.description: Regular users see only the dashboard and their account, and every administrator page and API refuses them
steps: Sign in as a regular user: the navigation offers Dashboard and Account only
An administrator page redirects to the dashboard, and no administrator request is sent
Every administrator route of the API answers 403 to a regular user and 401 without a token

features.description: An administrator creates, edits and deletes users on the Users page
steps: Open Users and add a user with a valid name and a password: the user is listed with its role
Edit the user's role or password
A name that breaks the name rule, or exists in another case, is refused with the reason
Delete the user: the request carries the name, and a list loaded before the id named someone else deletes nobody
features.notes: The steps use a user without SMB, so they make no host-level change. For a user with SMB the same edits reach the host: shares.smb-accounts and shares.password-follows-unos cover that.

features.description: A user changes their own password on the Account page
steps: On the Account page, enter the current password and the new one: the change is confirmed
The fields are reached through their labels, and a missing field is refused
Warnings of the answer, for example about SMB, are shown until dismissed
The old password no longer signs in, and the new one does
features.notes: webui/tests/change-password.spec.ts on the stand-in's real supervisor, for a regular test user without SMB. Step 2: the three fields are filled through their labels, and with any one of them empty the browser reports it missing and sends nothing. Step 1: with all three the page says "Password changed successfully" and clears the form. Step 4: after Logout the old password answers "Incorrect username or password" and the new one opens the dashboard. Step 3: account-smb.spec.ts shows the warnings of an answer until Dismiss, with a canned answer because ending SMB sessions needs Samba; test_smb_accounts.py makes the server send them. TestPasswordChange of test_smb_accounts.py signs in with the old and the new password after a change, with and without an active SMB account, and refuses a request that lacks a field (422). Without SMB the change is database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md); Samba's copy of an active account is shares.password-follows-unos. The server takes a new password of any length from a user without SMB: the 8 characters are the page's rule. Sessions signed in before the change stay valid (auth.session-revocation).

features.description: A user creates API tokens for scripts, and a token can be disabled, expires and can be deleted
steps: POST /api/v1/auth/tokens with a name and a lifetime returns the token once
A request with Authorization: Bearer <token> is accepted with the rights of the token's owner
POST /api/v1/auth/tokens/{id}/toggle disables it, and its requests answer 401
An expired token answers 401
Tokens of another user can be neither seen nor deleted
A request made with an API token cannot create, toggle or delete tokens: it answers 403
A name has 1 to 64 characters and the permissions are *, and a user has at most 100 tokens: more answers 422 or 409
features.notes: Step 1: TestApiTokenUse in test_authz.py creates a token with a name and a lifetime of 30 days: the answer holds it, GET /auth/tokens never does, and the database keeps only its SHA-256 (ADR-0239); TestApiTokenExpiry bounds the lifetime (ADR-0027). Step 2: a regular user's token gets 403 from the administrator-only APIs, and an administrator's token reaches them. Step 3: after POST /auth/tokens/{id}/toggle its requests answer 401 'API token is disabled' until it is toggled back; test_ws_auth.py refuses a disabled token at the WebSocket and closes a socket whose token is disabled. Step 4: a token whose expires_at has passed answers 401 'API token has expired', from the second after it. Step 5: TestApiTokenOwnership and TestApiTokenUse: another user, an administrator too, can neither list, toggle nor delete it, also with a token of their own. Steps 6 and 7 (ADR-0253, after the review of 2026-11-07): TestApiTokensAreManagedWithASession (a token, an administrator's too, gets 403 on create, toggle and delete, also of itself, and can still list; an invalid or disabled one keeps its 401) and TestApiTokenBounds (an empty, blank, 65-character or 900000-character name, other permissions than * and no name answer 422 and store nothing; the 101st token of a user answers 409, also for two requests at the same moment). api-tokens.spec.ts runs steps 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 and the name bounds against the stand-in's real supervisor; step 4 and the limit of 100 are backend-only, because the shortest lifetime is a day. Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md). API only: no page manages tokens. The permissions field takes only * until scopes are checked (auth.api-token-scopes).

features.description: A user sees the recent sign-ins of their account with the client's real address
steps: Sign in from a client: System > Security > Login History lists it with its time and the client's address, not the proxy's
Failed sign-ins are listed as failed
features.notes: webui/tests/login-history.spec.ts on the stand-in's real supervisor, for a regular test user, with the browser in Asia/Kathmandu (UTC+05:45): a wrong password, then the right one. Login History, once loaded, lists exactly those two, newest first: SUCCESS, then FAILED with "Incorrect username or password", each with the time of its sign-in in the browser's time zone and the address that the server recorded for the test process's own sign-in through the API from the same machine (127.0.0.1 and ::1 count as one), and the counts 2, 1 and 1 (steps 1 and 2). On the compose test stack that address is the test-runner's, and the spec also checks that it is not the proxy's (Caddy, the host webui). Fixed with it (ADR-0262): the times were answered without their UTC offset and shown hours off, the attempts of one second came in any order, and clearing the history counted its days in the server's local time. On the stand-in the browser and the proxy share an address; that the list shows the browser's address and not the proxy's is TestRealClientAddress of test_authz.py, through the proxy layer of deploy/docker-compose.yml. The history is kept by name: a regular user sees the attempts on their name since their account was created (ADR-0263), so a user created again with the name of a deleted one does not see that account's rows, which administrators still see (TestLoginHistory). A history that cannot be loaded is reported with its reason and Retry, not shown as empty with counts of 0 (security.spec.ts). DELETE /api/v1/security/login-history takes older_than_days from 0 to 36500 and answers 422 otherwise. Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md).

features.description: Live data needs a signed-in session: the WebSocket authenticates with its first message, never with a token in the URL
steps: The dashboard opens /ws/v1/events and sends {"type": "auth", "token": ...} first, and stats follow
A token in the URL, a forged token or no token closes the socket with code 4401
A session that ends while the socket is open closes the socket

features.description: Each installation signs its sessions with a secret of its own, and published placeholder secrets are refused
steps: A supervisor started without UNOS_JWT_SECRET makes /data/jwt_secret with mode 0600 and keeps it across restarts
A token signed with a secret this repository once published answers 401
UNOS_JWT_SECRET set to a published placeholder stops the supervisor at startup

features.description: A user with two-factor authentication keeps recovery codes and signs in with one when the authenticator is lost
steps: On the Account page, generate ten recovery codes: they are shown once
At the code step of the sign-in, a recovery code opens the session, and the same code never works again
The Account page shows how many codes are left
features.notes: Against the stand-in's real supervisor, recovery-codes.spec.ts generates ten codes on the Account page, which a reload no longer shows and of which one signs in (step 1), signs in at the code step with a code that a second time answers 'Invalid recovery code' (step 2), and reads 10, 9 and 8 codes left (step 3). It also checks what a failed generation says: no codes were generated after a refusal, and after a lost answer that the saved codes may no longer work. test_recovery_codes.py adds two sign-ins with one code at the same moment, codes typed in any case or without dashes, new codes generated meanwhile, codes removed with two-factor authentication also when a generation commits while it is being turned off, and codes answered when their audit entry cannot be written. Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md). Turning 2FA off still needs a code of the authenticator app, and no administrator can reset 2FA.

features.description: An administrator requires two-factor authentication for every account, with a grace period to set it up
steps: Turn on the requirement: accounts without two-factor authentication are asked to set it up at their next sign-in
After the grace period such an account can only set up two-factor authentication

features.description: A user signs in with a hardware security key (WebAuthn) as the second factor
steps: On the Account page, register a security key
At the code step of the sign-in, touching the key opens the session

features.description: Signing out, a password change or an administrator's revoke ends a session on the server
steps: After sign-out, the session's token answers 401
A password change ends the user's other sessions
An administrator ends a user's sessions on the Users page
features.notes: Today sign-out only clears the browser's copy of the token.

features.description: The web UI keeps its session token out of localStorage
steps: After sign-in, localStorage holds no token
A reload keeps the session, or asks to sign in again, as the chosen design says
features.notes: Needs an ADR on the storage; cookies conflict with ADR-0009.

features.description: An API token can be limited to reading, or to named areas of the API
steps: Create a read-only token: GET requests work and changes answer 403
A token limited to an area answers 403 outside it

features.description: An API token's last use is stored at most once an hour, so automations do not write to the system disk on every request
steps: A script makes 100 requests with one token within a minute: last_used_at is committed at most once
GET /api/v1/auth/tokens shows a last use at most an hour old
On the dev device the requests of an automation write next to nothing to the SD card (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0252, which superseded ADR-0191): verify_api_token commits last_used_at only when it is empty or an hour old, and a commit that fails is logged and the request answered. Steps 1 and 2 pass: test_api_token_last_use.py (100 requests within a minute commit once, the next commit comes once the stored use is an hour old, GET /auth/tokens shows a last use at most an hour old, a request's own commit does not write a skipped last use, and a commit that fails at the UPDATE or at the COMMIT is rolled back and the request answered), test_ws_auth.py (the WebSocket's re-checks commit once; a handshake and a re-check whose commit fails still pass, and the socket stays open) and api-tokens.spec.ts on the stand-in (the last use the API shows stays as it is after more requests). Open: step 3, the device check after the deploy, with scripts/dev/sd.sh measure (ADR-0214): 100 requests within a minute with one API token, such as GET /api/v1/auth/me, write about what 100 requests with a session token write, plus at most one SQLite commit for the first (about 0.15 MiB, ADR-0224); before the change each of them committed. Database only: not host-level (GLOSSARY.md).

features.description: Users can sign in while the disk that holds /data is full
steps: Fill the filesystem of /data, then sign in: the sign-in works
The audit entry that could not be written is reported in the log
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0251): record_login_attempt rolls back a commit that fails with an OperationalError and logs the attempt as JSON, log_action logs an entry whose append fails with OSError as its JSON line, and login answers either way. test_sign_in_full_disk.py makes /data full by fault injection: SQLite's own 'database or disk is full' (PRAGMA max_page_count, login_attempts filled to its last page), the audit append failing with ENOSPC, and a commit failing at its end. Step 1: the sign-in answers a session token that GET /auth/me accepts, a wrong password 401, the password with a TOTP code its token, a wrong code 401. Step 2: the audit entry and the login attempt it could not write are logged at ERROR as JSON, with the user, the client address, the time (UTC for the attempt, whose row takes its time from the database) and the error; record_login_attempt rolls its session back, so that the caller can go on using it (TestRecordLoginAttempt). A recovery code does not sign in while its use cannot be stored: 500, and the code stays unused. Not host-level (GLOSSARY.md), and the dev device's /data is never filled for a check (ADR-0214). On a system disk full to the last block, the container's json-file log on the same disk can lose those lines too (ADR-0178).

features.description: Passwords are checked as given: the cut to 72 bytes kept for hashes of the passlib-era code is gone
steps: verify_password in supervisor/src/auth/utils.py checks the whole password, without cutting it to 72 bytes first
A sign-in with a password longer than 72 bytes fails like a wrong password, without a server error
New passwords longer than 72 bytes are still refused with 422, and the comment in supervisor/src/auth/schemas.py no longer points to old hashes

features.description: An administrator renames a user, and the user's SMB access follows the new name
steps: Edit a user and change the name: the user signs in with the new name, and the old one is refused
A user with SMB keeps it under the new name: Samba's account of the old name is removed, and the one of the new name is made with the password that the rename asks for
A new name that breaks the name rule, or exists in another case, is refused with the reason
features.notes: Today PUT /auth/users/{id} answers 409 for another name (ADR-0116).

features.description: The Storage page lists the host's disks with what UNOS knows about each
steps: Open Storage: every whole disk of the host is listed with model, size and serial
Each disk says whether it is the system disk, in use or holding data, and which pool it belongs to
When the disks cannot be listed, the page says why
features.notes: Proven here, 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_disk_safety.py TestDisksEndpoint (test_lists_every_whole_disk_with_model_size_and_serial: GET /api/v1/storage/disks lists every whole disk with model, size and serial, without the boot SD card and zram) and TestListDisks (hidden boot and virtual devices, a system disk on NVMe, a root shown as /dev/root, old lsblk); storage.spec.ts 'every disk is listed with its model, serial and size, and what uses it' (each row's device, model and serial, size, HDD or SSD, contents, mountpoints and status, on route fakes with the supervisor's texts). Step 2: TestDisksEndpoint test_each_disk_says_what_uses_it_and_which_pool_it_belongs_to (system, in use with its reason, holding data, the pool of a disk and of both members of a mounted pool) and TestListDisks (swap, md, wipefs signatures, a failed probe counts as data); the same spec shows the System, In use, Pool, Has data and Free badges with the reasons. Step 3: test_a_disk_list_that_cannot_be_read_answers_500_with_the_reason (500 'lsblk failed: <reason>') and the specs 'a disk list that cannot be loaded says why, and the pools are still shown' and 'a pool list that cannot be loaded says why, and the disks are still shown' (ADR-0271: each card says why instead of 'No disks found'). The steps only read the host (lsblk, findmnt, swapon and wipefs --no-act through supervisor/src/host.py), so they make no host-level change and need no reboot check; the device check was done on 2026-11-06. A sanity check after the next deploy: Storage on the device lists /dev/sda with its model, serial and size and the badge of the pool data's disk, and the SD card is not listed. Reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08: no finding left open for this entry.

features.description: An administrator creates a btrfs pool from free disks with a RAID profile, after typed confirmations
steps: Select free disks, a name and a profile: single, RAID0, RAID1, RAID1C3, RAID1C4 or RAID10, never RAID5 or RAID6
Create stays disabled until the pool name is typed, and for disks with data until the erase is confirmed
The system disk and disks in use are not offered, and a disk whose serial, WWN or size changed since it was selected is refused and the list reloaded
The new pool is mounted at /mnt/pools/<name> by UUID with a managed fstab entry and listed as healthy
features.notes: Not run on the dev device: it needs a spare disk. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator unmounts and mounts a pool, and a pool comes back mounted after a reboot
steps: Unmount a pool after the confirmation: it shows not mounted, and nothing can be written into its empty mountpoint, not even by root
Mount it again: the managed fstab entry (# unos-pool:<name>) is back, and the pool is healthy
Reboot the host: the pool is mounted before Docker starts, and the apps on it start
Unmount is refused while running apps keep data on the pool
features.notes: Built and proven here on 2026-11-07: storage.spec.ts 'Pool unmount, mount and removal (fake data)' on route fakes that change their pools as the supervisor does: Unmount asks first (Cancel sends nothing), POST /pools/<name>/unmount, then the card shows Not mounted, no fstab badge and no Scrub, Volumes or Unmount; Mount sends POST /mount and the card shows Healthy, Mounted at boot and its mountpoint again; the 409s of a pool that running apps or host processes use are shown in the dialog and the pool stays mounted. test_pool_persistence.py pins those 409 texts at the API (TestPoolEndpoints test_a_pool_that_running_apps_use_answers_which_ones, test_a_pool_that_host_processes_use_answers_409) and proves the host side on the fake host: the guard chattr +i, the managed entry removed and written again, the startup reconcile (TestUnmountAndDelete, TestMountPool, TestReconcile, TestAppChecksBeforeStart, TestLifespanRunsReconcile). Device check: 2026-11-05 (Phase 0 deploy: unmount, mount and a reboot of that tree); the deployed tree changed since. Device check 2026-11-08: every unmount of the pool data answered 409 "still in use outside the host ... so it was mounted again", also with every app stopped: systemd-resolved, -timesyncd, -udevd, -networkd, rsyslogd and -logind run with sandboxing in mount namespaces of their own, each with a copy of the pool's mount in a peer group of its own, which the host's umount does not reach; UNOS mounted the pool again, as designed. Built (ADR-0288): after the host's umount, the copies (the pool's filesystem by MAJ:MIN at its mountpoint with the host mount's root, in a namespace whose own root is the host's: the same MAJ:MIN and FSROOT at /, as systemd makes them for services) are unmounted with umount --namespace <pid>, never lazily; a namespace that has the pool mounted anywhere else (a container's bind mount), has it mounted at all while its root is its own (a container, also one that binds /mnt/pools or /mnt and so keeps the pool's mount at its mountpoint for its apps), or has another filesystem at its mountpoint together with a copy, is refused with 409 that names the process, and the pool is mounted again, as when a copy cannot be unmounted or the filesystem is still active after them. Tested in test_pool_persistence.py (the mount namespaces of the FakeHost: service copies, stacked copies, peers, an exited process, bind mounts, containers with the pool at its mountpoint, also while Docker cannot be asked, namespaces with roots of their own, a busy or hanging umount, lsns failing; the endpoints and their smb.conf applies; the texts of storage-fakes.ts), test_smb_integration.py (the shares stop being served) and storage.spec.ts ('an unmount refused while apps use the pool says why, and the pool stays mounted': a refusal for running containers, then for a mount namespace that has the pool mounted elsewhere, shown in the dialog while the pool stays mounted). Open: the device check after a deploy and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). With transmission stopped, Unmount data on the Storage page answers 200 and shows Not mounted, and GET /api/v1/storage/pools shows mounted false and persistent false; on the host, findmnt lists nothing at /mnt/pools/data, /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid> is gone (this decides), no line of /proc/*/mountinfo lists the pool's MAJ:MIN with the filesystem type btrfs (the field after ' - '; the number alone can belong to a tmpfs or overlay mounted after the pool's was freed), the supervisor's log has "Unmounted /mnt/pools/data in the mount namespaces of processes ..., which kept copies of its mount", lsattr -d /mnt/pools/data shows the i flag and touch /mnt/pools/data/x as root fails with 'Operation not permitted', and /etc/fstab has no '# unos-pool:data' marker. Should Unmount answer 409 that names a process of a sandboxed service as having the pool mounted at /mnt/pools/data, compare findmnt --task <pid> --mountpoint / -o MAJ:MIN,FSROOT with findmnt --mountpoint / -o MAJ:MIN,FSROOT on the host: copies are unmounted only where the two agree. Mount data: the marker and its entry are back, the pool is Healthy, and transmission starts. With transmission running, Unmount answers 409 that names transmission, and the pool stays mounted. After the owner's reboot the pool data is mounted at /mnt/pools/data before docker.service starts (systemd-analyze critical-chain docker.service lists mnt-pools-data.mount), and transmission runs. Report the SD MiB of each step. Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy of main 533668a (the fix of ADR-0288): with transmission running, Unmount answered 409 naming it and the pool stayed mounted; with it stopped, Unmount answered 200, the supervisor unmounted a service's copy of the mount, and the host had nothing at /mnt/pools/data, no /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>, no '# unos-pool:data' marker, and touch in the mountpoint failed (Operation not permitted); Mount brought the marker back, the pool was healthy, and transmission started. After a reboot from the API the pool was mounted and transmission ran.

features.description: Storage and the dashboard show each pool's health as the host reports it, and a degraded pool raises an alert
steps: A mounted pool without errors shows healthy
An unmounted pool shows not mounted, and one whose state cannot be read shows unknown, never healthy
Missing devices, error counters, a read-only mount and a filesystem that btrfs forced read-only are shown on the pool
Detach a device of a RAID1 test pool: within 5 minutes the RAID monitor marks it degraded and sends an alert that names the cause
GET /api/v1/health/raid-monitor/status shows the time of the latest check
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-05 (a healthy pool, also after a reboot of the Phase 0 tree). The degraded case needs a test pool on spare disks. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC): the pool data shows healthy and mounted read-write, and GET /api/v1/health/raid-monitor/status names its latest check (23:00:15 UTC, after the boot). Open: step 4, a degraded RAID1 test pool, which needs spare disks and was never checked on the device.

features.description: An administrator removes a pool from UNOS after typing its name, and its disks keep their data
steps: Delete asks for the pool's name, unmounts the pool and drops its managed fstab entry and empty mountpoint
The disks are not touched: the filesystem is listed again as an unmounted pool that can be mounted later
A pool that host processes or containers use is refused with 409
features.notes: Built and proven here on 2026-11-07: storage.spec.ts 'remove pool asks for its name, and the disks keep the pool to mount later' (the trash button 'Remove pool <name>', Continue, Remove Pool disabled until the exact name is typed, DELETE /pools/<name>, then the pool listed again as Not mounted with Mount, which mounts it again) and 'a pool in use is not removed, and the dialog says why' (the 409 in the dialog, the pool still mounted). test_pool_persistence.py: test_delete_forgets_the_pool_but_keeps_the_data (umount, the managed entry dropped, chattr -i and rmdir of the mountpoint, no mkfs or wipefs, listed again as unmounted and mountable), test_delete_keeps_a_non_empty_directory_guarded, test_delete_is_non_destructive, and the 409s at the API for containers and host processes (TestPoolEndpoints). The API takes no typed name: only the page asks for it (ADR-0035). Built: Remove Pool unmounts through the code of Unmount, so the copies that services with sandboxing keep in their mount namespaces, whose root is the host's, are unmounted with it, and a namespace that has the pool mounted anywhere else, or at all while its root is its own, like a container's that binds /mnt/pools, is refused with 409 (ADR-0288). storage.spec.ts 'a removal refused while the pool is in use says why, and the pool stays' shows that 409 in the dialog while the pool stays. test_pool_persistence.py tests the server: the managed fstab entry and the empty mountpoint dropped, the disks untouched and the filesystem listed again, the refusals while containers (also one whose namespace keeps the pool at its mountpoint), host processes or other mount namespaces use the pool; test_smb_integration.py its shares. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), on the device on a test pool of spare disks, not the pool data. Remove Pool (typing its name) answers 200; /etc/fstab has no '# unos-pool:<name>' line, /mnt/pools/<name> is gone, /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid> is gone (this decides), no line of /proc/*/mountinfo lists the pool's MAJ:MIN with the filesystem type btrfs (the field after ' - '; the number alone can belong to a tmpfs or overlay mounted after the pool's was freed), btrfs filesystem show still lists the filesystem, and the Storage page lists it as Not mounted; Mount mounts it again with its data and marker. With a container using the pool, Remove Pool answers 409 that names it, and the fstab entry stays. After the owner's reboot a removed pool is not mounted. Report the SD MiB of each step.

features.description: An administrator lists, creates and deletes the volumes of a mounted pool
steps: Open a mounted pool's Volumes dialog: the subvolumes in its top folder are listed, without snapshots
Create a volume with an optional quota: it appears at /mnt/pools/<pool>/<name>
Delete asks for the name; a volume that apps, Docker volumes, shares or NFS exports use is refused with what uses it
On a pool mounted read-only the dialog lists the volumes and says why they cannot change
features.notes: Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy). 2026-11-07: the Volumes dialog sends the optional quota, typed in GiB, in bytes and shows the 409 when quotas are not enabled (ADR-0243, which superseded ADR-0241; storage.spec.ts). Open: the device check of a create with a quota (the 409 while quotas are off on the pool data; once the owner enabled them, the limit on the new volume's quota group) and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check 2026-11-07 on the pool data: a volume with a quota was refused with the hint (409, quotas are off on data), the same volume without a quota was created at /mnt/pools/data/unoscheck, listed and deleted.

features.description: An administrator creates, lists, restores and deletes read-only snapshots, also on a schedule with a keep count
steps: On Snapshots, create a snapshot of a pool or a volume: it is listed with its time
Restore a snapshot: its content comes back as a new folder next to the original
Delete a snapshot
A scheduled snapshot task with keep count 3 keeps the three newest automatic snapshots and deletes no other
A scheduled snapshot of a pool that is not mounted fails with Pool <name> is not mounted
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0243, which superseded ADR-0241): GET /snapshots/subvolumes lists each mounted pool and its volumes, read through src/host.py, a pool whose volumes cannot be read alone with volumes_error, and the Snapshots page picks one; times come in UTC with their offset, the names snap_, restore_ and auto_ take UTC, the list runs no du and needs its pool or volume, and create, restore and delete use dialogs. Create, restore and delete, the scheduled ones included, act on the folders they opened, through /proc/self/fd paths, and delete by subvolume id (ADR-0242). Asserted on fakes: steps 1 to 3 by test_snapshots.py and snapshots.spec.ts, steps 4 and 5 by test_scheduler_validation.py and scheduler.spec.ts. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step; it is also the first run of the real btrfs-progs with /proc/self/fd paths, subvolid-resolve and delete --subvolid: GET /snapshots/subvolumes lists /mnt/pools/data and its volumes; a snapshot of a volume and one of the pool are listed with their local time; restoring the pool's snapshot makes the volume restore_<time>, which the Volumes dialog deletes (a volume's copy stays undeletable in the web UI, storage.restore-copies-deletable); delete removes a snapshot; a snapshot task with keep count 3 run four times keeps three auto_ snapshots; a run while the pool is unmounted fails with Pool data is not mounted. Device check 2026-11-07 on the pool data: a volume was offered on Snapshots, snapshotted (listed with its UTC time), restored into restore_<time> with its content, and the snapshot deleted; a snapshot task with keep count 3 run four times kept the three newest auto_ snapshots and deleted no other (0.031 and 0.164 MiB on the SD card). Step 5 (a pool that is not mounted) is proven by test_snapshot_task_requires_mounted_pool: the only pool is in use by transmission.

features.description: An administrator scrubs a mounted pool, follows the progress and cancels it, also on a schedule
steps: Start Scrub on a mounted pool: the request returns once btrfs has started, and the API stays responsive
The pool shows the scrub's progress and, at the end, its result
Cancel stops a running scrub
A scheduled scrub task scrubs its pool, and fails without running btrfs when the pool is not mounted
A pool that is not mounted offers no Scrub button
features.notes: Built and proven here on 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_storage.py TestScrubStart (the request answers once btrfs returns, the scrub process still running), TestScrubOffTheEventLoop (worker threads, timeouts). Step 2: TestScrubStatus (btrfs-progs 6 output parsed: progress while it runs, finished, every error of the error summary summed, aborted, interrupted, never scrubbed) and storage.spec.ts 'Scrub (fake data)': Start Scrub, the progress bar 'Scrub progress' with bytes, percent, rate and duration, updated every 2 seconds, then 'Last scrub: No errors' with the start time; 'Last scrub: 13 error(s)' and the interrupted result (ADR-0272). Step 3: TestScrubStatus test_cancel_answers_the_cancelled_scrub and the spec 'cancel stops a running scrub, and the result says it was cancelled' (DELETE, followed while btrfs still reports running, then 'Last scrub: cancelled before it finished'). A status btrfs cannot report answers 500, not idle (test_a_status_that_btrfs_cannot_report_is_an_error_not_idle), and the card then says 'Could not read the scrub status' instead of a stale progress and still offers Cancel Scrub (spec 'a scrub status that cannot be read says why instead of a stale progress'); a start or cancel that btrfs did is answered running or aborted when the status read after it fails (test_a_start_or_cancel_whose_status_cannot_be_read). Step 4: test_scheduler_validation.py test_scrub_task, test_scrub_of_an_unmounted_pool_fails_without_btrfs, test_a_scheduled_scrub_is_recorded_when_btrfs_returns. Step 5: storage.spec.ts 'shows pool health and mount state' and the unmount spec (no Scrub on a pool that is not mounted). The 409 of the API for an unmounted pool is storage.scrub-needs-mounted-pool. Open, on the device, on the pool data: Scrub on the Storage page shows the progress moving and a result at the end ('Last scrub: No errors' on a healthy pool), Cancel Scrub on a second run shows 'Last scrub: cancelled before it finished', a scheduled scrub task's Run now is recorded as success, the API answers other requests meanwhile, and the SD writes of the run are measured (the scrub status lives in the /var/lib/btrfs tmpfs, ADR-0171); and the re-check after the owner's reboot (ADR-0018), after which the pool shows no last scrub result: the restart forgot it (ADR-0171). Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy of main 1fdf802: a scrub of the pool data ran to the end in 19 s with 0 errors and its progress moving; a second scrub was cancelled (aborted). Right after the start, GET .../scrub still says idle for a moment. The re-check of 2026-11-09 (PROGRESS.md, Log) found step 2 failing on the device: for about 6 s after Start Scrub the API answered idle, Start Scrub's own answer too, until btrfs had recorded the new scrub, so the page stopped following a scrub that ran and offered Scrub again. Open: a fix, and its device check before and after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator reads the SMART data of every disk the Storage page lists and schedules SMART tests
steps: On Storage or System > Disk Health, open a disk: its SMART attributes, temperature and overall health are shown
Disk Health lists the same disks as Storage, NVMe included, and disks without SMART data too
A partition or another device is refused as not a disk of this system
In System > Scheduler, a SMART test task offers the connected whole disks and keeps the disk of a task while it is disconnected
Run now records the run as success, failed or timed out
features.notes: Disk Health opens each disk's SMART data in a dialog, from what GET /health/disks returned (ADR-0235): health, temperature, power-on hours and cycles, serial, firmware, the last self-test (of the ATA or the NVMe self-test log), the ATA attributes with their status, and the SMART/Health Information log of NVMe disks (test_health_smart.py, health.spec.ts on route fakes). smartctl runs in the container (architecture.host-command-layer), and GET /health/disks runs it without -n standby, so opening Disk Health wakes sleeping disks (storage.disk-spindown). Device check: 2026-11-06 (slice 1 deploy: SMART data and a short test of the pool's disk). Open: the device check of the dialog (System > Disk Health on the device: the pool's disk /dev/sda opens with its attributes, temperature and PASSED; an NVMe disk, if one is connected, with its health log) and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). Device check 2026-11-07 after the deploy of main cce0def: GET /api/v1/health/disks returned the SMART data of /dev/sda (WDC WD6400AACS: health PASSED, 33 C, 51832 power-on hours, 17 attributes, the last short self-test), and again after a reboot.

features.description: SMART attributes are recorded over time, and a rising count of reallocated or pending sectors raises an alert
steps: The SMART monitor records each disk's attributes at every pass
A rise in reallocated or pending sectors sends an alert to the e-mail and Telegram channels
GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends and /smart/predictions report the trend and a failure estimate per disk
features.notes: Proven here, 2026-11-07. Step 1: test_health_monitor.py TestSmartHistoryWrites test_every_pass_is_recorded_in_ram_where_the_endpoints_read_it (each pass adds the disk's counters, temperature and path, as /smart/history, /smart-monitor/status and /smart/trends report), test_health_smart.py test_the_monitor_checks_the_same_disks (every awake whole disk of Disk Health) and test_storage.py test_monitor_round_runs_in_a_worker_thread. The history is written only when a pass changes it and at shutdown (ADR-0269, ADR-0214): TestSmartHistoryWrites proves that passes that change nothing and a start that changes nothing write nothing, that a new disk, a counter, a path or an lsblk serial writes it at once, that a failed write is tried again and the alert still sent, and that the snapshots in RAM are written at shutdown. Step 2: TestSmartAlertChannels (a rise of the reallocated or of the pending sectors reaches every enabled e-mail and Telegram channel once, not a disabled one, with the title, message and recommendation) and TestSmartTrendAlerts (one alert per rise, again for a further rise, none after a snapshot without the counters, again for a rise after a drop, ADR-0270); TestSmartHistoryWrites test_a_pass_that_ends_after_the_shutdown_keeps_nothing_and_alerts_at_the_next_start (ADR-0269; an alert still being sent when the supervisor stops is cut off, as before); test_storage.py TestAlertsOffTheEventLoop (delivery off the event loop, bounded). Step 3: TestSmartTrendsEndpoint (GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends lists every tracked disk with its data points and rising counters, steady and removed disks included, the disks without a serial or with an empty one by path, the window of the last 24 values, ADR-0270) and test_smart_predictions.py (GET /smart/predictions: the failure estimate of each connected disk, ADR-0235). Only the ATA counters are recorded, so NVMe disks have none, and sleeping disks are skipped (smartctl -n standby). No host-level change. A sanity check after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/health/smart/trends lists the device's disks with data_points growing by one per hour, and /data/smart_history.json keeps its mtime across hourly passes (stat), so the hourly SD writes of the old monitor are gone (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure over a pass). Reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08; the findings were fixed except two, recorded in ADR-0269 and ADR-0270: an alert still being sent when the supervisor stops is cut off and not sent again (the monitor writes before it sends, as before), and a history that an older monitor stored under an empty serial is not continued under 'unknown'.

features.description: Disks whose SMART trend predicts a failure are marked replace soon on the dashboard and in Disk Health
steps: A disk with a predicted failure shows replace soon with the reason
The mark goes away when the prediction does
features.notes: GET /health/smart/predictions scores the SMART history as ADR-0235 fixes it (the rate over the last 24 snapshots; no prediction for NVMe disks or the shared 'unknown' history) and covers the disks connected now, found by the lsblk serial the monitor stores with each snapshot when it names one disk and one history, else by path. A counter is read from the snapshots that hold it, and the history file is written atomically; one that cannot be read answers 500. Disk Health marks a disk Replace soon by its serial, with the risk factors and the recommendation, and lists a prediction that matches no listed disk apart; the dashboard lists such disks for administrators and links to Disk Health; both say when the predictions cannot be read. Proven here, 2026-11-07: test_smart_predictions.py (the threshold, the window, snapshots without the counters, the disks covered, the mark going a day after the last rise, the history file), health.spec.ts and dashboard.spec.ts on route fakes, roles.spec.ts (no request for regular users); reviewed in a fresh context twice (ADR-0017), the findings of the second fixed on 2026-11-07. No host-level change, and no failing disk can be shown on the device. A sanity check there after the next deploy: GET /api/v1/health/smart/predictions answers 200 for the connected disks, new snapshots in /data/smart_history.json hold lsblk_serial, and the dashboard shows no mark and no warning.

features.description: The Snapshots page lists the copies that snapshot restores made, and deletes them
steps: Restore a snapshot of a volume: the copy restore_<time> is listed on the Snapshots page
Delete it there after the check that nothing uses it: the subvolume is removed by its subvolume id
The volume that held it can be deleted afterwards

features.description: Starting a scrub of a pool that is not mounted answers 409, and one helper starts every scrub

features.description: A btrfs or smartctl command that hangs in the kernel no longer holds a worker thread after its timeout
steps: A scrub, stats reset or SMART test command that does not return is killed at its timeout, and its worker thread is free at once
The API answers the timeout, and later requests are served
features.notes: Built (ADR-0290, which superseded ADR-0289 after the review): btrfs scrub start, status and cancel (the Storage page and scheduled scrubs), btrfs device stats --reset, smartctl -t (POST /api/v1/health/disk/{device}/test and scheduled SMART tests), the reads of SMART data (Disk Health, the Storage page's SMART data and the hourly SMART monitor) and the btrfs subvolume show of the scheduler's snapshot cleanup (which had no timeout and now has 60 seconds) run through host.run_in_container. It starts the command in a session of its own; at the timeout it kills the command's process group with SIGKILL, leaves the wait for its end to a daemon thread and raises TimeoutExpired at once. It runs one run of a command at a time: a second run waits for the first and starts once it ended, and while a killed run is still stuck the command is not started but fails at once, logged once as "Not started", so a hung pool or disk keeps at most one stuck process of each command. A SMART test without an answer now says "smartctl did not answer within 30 seconds: <device> may not be responding" instead of "Command timed out"; a snapshot cleanup whose btrfs does not answer deletes nothing, and the snapshot task's run fails with "Snapshot <name> created, but old snapshots were not cleaned up: btrfs did not answer within 60 seconds. The pool may not be responding.". Step 1: tests/test_command_timeouts.py: TestRealProcesses (a timeout ends the command and the sleep it started, as nsenter starts its command, and no other process; a session of its own) and TestCommandsThatDoNotReturn (with fake processes whose wait never returns: the timeout raised at once, the process group killed, the wait left to a daemon thread, a stuck command not started again, a second run that waits for the first until it is killed and then starts nothing, a second run that starts as soon as the first answered); TestScrubStart of test_storage.py and test_a_scheduled_scrub_is_recorded_when_btrfs_returns of test_scheduler_validation.py run fake btrfs scripts through the real runner. Step 2: tests/test_command_timeouts.py through the API with one worker thread of each kind: POST, GET and DELETE /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub, POST /api/v1/health/raid/<pool>/reset-stats, POST /api/v1/health/disk/<disk>/test, GET /api/v1/storage/disks/<disk>/smart, GET /api/v1/health/disk/<disk> and GET /api/v1/health/disks answer the timeout, then serve the next request at once, and answer at once while the command is stuck; a scheduled scrub and SMART test fail with their message and free the scheduler's thread, a scheduled snapshot task whose cleanup gets no answer fails and keeps the snapshots, and the SMART monitor records the other disks; test_a_stats_reset_that_does_not_return_answers_500 of test_health_monitor.py; test_a_snapshot_task_whose_cleanup_btrfs_does_not_answer_is_recorded_as_failed of test_scheduler_validation.py (the run and the task's last status are failed). Open, because scrubs and SMART reach the host's pools and disks (a host-level change): the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214). On the dev device: POST /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub answers 200 within seconds, GET /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub then says running and `ps -o pid,sid,pgid,args` shows the scrub's btrfs process with its own session, and DELETE /api/v1/storage/pools/<pool>/scrub cancels it; POST /api/v1/health/raid/<pool>/reset-stats answers 200; POST /api/v1/health/disk/<disk>/test?test_type=short answers started; GET /api/v1/health/disks, GET /api/v1/health/disk/<disk> and GET /api/v1/storage/disks/<disk>/smart answer with the disk's data; Run now of a BTRFS Scrub, a SMART Test and a BTRFS Snapshot task with a keep count records success; `docker logs unos-supervisor` has neither a "Killed" nor a "Not started" warning; and after a reboot the same. A process stuck in the kernel cannot be made on the device on purpose: that part is shown by the fakes only. Not covered: the Snapshots page's commands (run_cmd of src/snapshots/router.py, also the scheduled snapshot itself) still use subprocess.run, since they name their folders by descriptor numbers and their list would have to stop at the first btrfs that does not answer; the Storage page's scrub status polling does not wait for each answer, so on a hung pool its overlapping requests hold the default executor's threads for one timeout (docs/USER_GUIDE.md says so), after which the card says 'Could not read the scrub status' with the timeout (ADR-0272); the commands of host.run_on_host still run on, on the host, after their timeout, which frees the thread (architecture.host-command-layer).

After the deploy of main ebb1856: an export of /mnt/pools/data/shared for 10.1.1.0/24, read only, was written to /etc/exports.d/unos.exports with mp=/mnt/pools/data, exportfs -v listed it with root_squash and secure, GET /shares/nfs listed it as managed, the workstation's showmount -e listed it, and Delete removed the line and the export. After a reboot from the API nfs-server was active, exportfs -v listed the export with the pool mounted, and the client read the file again; Delete then removed the line, and exportfs -v no longer listed it. /etc/exports kept its bytes (sha256) through two adds and two deletes. features.description: The NAS appears in the network browsers of Windows (WS-Discovery) and macOS (Bonjour)
steps: Windows Explorer's Network view lists the NAS
The macOS Finder sidebar lists the NAS
NetBIOS can then be turned off
features.notes: Built (ADR-0275): the rendered [global] turns NetBIOS off (disable netbios = yes, smb ports = 445) and keeps smbd's Bonjour registration on (multicast dns register = yes). install.sh: start_samba enables and restarts smbd and turns nmbd off (systemctl disable --now nmbd); configure_discovery writes /etc/avahi/avahi-daemon.unos.conf (Debian's avahi-daemon settings with use-ipv6=no and publish-aaaa-on-ipv4=no), the drop-in avahi-daemon.service.d/unos.conf (avahi-daemon -s -f that file) and the drop-in wsdd2.service.d/unos.conf (wsdd2 -4), reloads systemd, installs avahi-daemon with --no-install-recommends (no libnss-mdns, which would change the host's name resolution) and enables and restarts it, then wsdd2 the same way when apt-cache show finds the package. Without one (Debian 11, Ubuntu without universe) it warns and the installation goes on; a package that exists but does not install stops it, with apt-get's error. Both services answer over IPv4 only: a Mac would otherwise connect from a global IPv6 address, which hosts allow refuses, and wsdd2's TCP ports would listen on tunnels (ADR-0227). wsdd2 is a reserved account name: wsdd2.service runs as the dynamic user wsdd2, which a static account of that name would replace. uninstall.sh enables nmbd again when it restores smb.conf.original and keeps avahi-daemon, wsdd2 and UNOS's files of both, none of them in /etc/unos. docs/INSTALL.md (Step 5, Network Discovery) and docs/USER_GUIDE.md (Finding the NAS) describe it. Tests: test_smbconf.py (TestGlobal: the three lines in both [global] variants); test_deploy_scripts.py (TestInstallScript: smbd without nmbd on a first installation and a rerun; neither avahi-daemon nor wsdd2 among install_dependencies' packages, avahi-daemon without what it recommends; avahi-daemon's settings and drop-in and wsdd2's drop-in written and loaded before the packages are installed; a missing wsdd2 package lets the installation go on, a package that fails to install stops it with apt-get's error; the order of main; TestUninstallScript: nmbd enabled again with the restored file, the completion; TestInstallGuide: the manual installation's packages, commands and files are those of install.sh); test_smb_models.py (wsdd2 is reserved). Not built: scripts/dev/check.sh still expects nmbd to be active and checks neither wsdd2 nor avahi-daemon (device.check-network-discovery). Open: steps 1 to 3 need the dev device and a Windows and a macOS computer on its LAN. On the device, in this order: deploy the branch while nmbd still runs, since check.sh needs it until device.check-network-discovery is done (smbd reloads the new smb.conf; nmbd keeps running until it is stopped); then the owner's actions (ADR-0211): the commands of docs/INSTALL.md Step 5 after the nmbd line (the three files, systemctl daemon-reload, avahi-daemon without recommends, wsdd2, enabling and restarting both), systemctl disable --now nmbd, and systemctl restart smbd (smb ports applies only at a restart). From then on, until device.check-network-discovery, check.sh reports nmbd inactive: its only expected problem. The device check, once device.check-network-discovery lets check.sh answer OK, and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes with scripts/dev/bin/testparm; systemctl is-active smbd wsdd2 avahi-daemon answers active for each, and nmbd is inactive and disabled; ss -tulpn lists no socket on UDP 137 or 138 or TCP 139, smbd on TCP 445, wsdd2 on UDP and TCP 3702 (and on 5355 where systemd-resolved does not hold it) and avahi-daemon on UDP 5353, with IPv4 sockets only; on a Windows computer of the LAN, File Explorer's Network view lists the NAS, and opening it there asks for a UNOS SMB account and then lists the shares it may use (steps 1 and 3); on a macOS computer of the LAN, dns-sd -G v4v6 <name>.local answers IPv4 addresses only, the Finder sidebar lists the NAS under Locations, once, and connecting from there with a UNOS SMB account lists its shares, also from a Mac with a global IPv6 address where the LAN gives it one (steps 2 and 3). features.description: Samba's own writes to the system disk are reduced: daemon logs in RAM, and no passdb write for a failed sign-in
steps: On a host whose /var/log is on the system disk, smbd and nmbd log to /run/samba with a small size cap
A failed SMB sign-in of an existing account writes nothing to passdb.tdb (scripts/dev/sd.sh measure)
features.notes: Built (ADR-0277, ADR-0278). Step 1: the rendered [global] has `log file = /run/samba/log.samba` and `max log size = 100` on every host, since RAM cannot be told from the system disk reliably (zram shows as a block device with ext4) and where /var/log is in RAM the file was in RAM already; one file for smbd, nmbd and the smbd of each client, without %m, so that clients add no files to /run. deploy/install.sh writes the same file. Tests: test_smbconf.py (TestGlobal), test_deploy_scripts.py; test_smbconf_testparm.py needs the device's testparm. Step 2: the account reconcile reads `pdbedit -P "password history"` at every start and sets it to 3 only when it differs, so that a wrong password that is one of an account's two previous passwords skips Samba's passdb write (test_smb_reconcile.py TestPasswordHistory and TestConsistent, against samba_fake.py). A password enters the history only when it is set while the policy is 3 (ADR-0278): an account whose password was set before, as every SMB account on the dev device, has an empty history, so its first change after the deploy does not spare retries of the password it replaced, and only its second change does. ADR-0159 and ADR-0278 took every other wrong password to write passdb.tdb once; measured on the device on 2026-11-09, none does while Samba's lockout policy is 0 (ADR-0310), so step 2 holds as written; limiting repeated failures is shares.smb-login-protection (ADR-0280). Unthrottled SMB sign-ins are an accepted risk (ADR-0280). Device check (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes against the device's testparm (scripts/dev/bin first on PATH); after the deploy, the reconcile's audit entry says "Set Samba's password history to 3 (it was 0)" once and `pdbedit -P "password history"` prints 3, and the next start reads it without setting it; after the apply's reload, /run/samba/log.samba exists and /var/log/samba/log.smbd and log.nmbd do not grow while clients connect, fail to sign in and Samba reloads; with an SMB account activated after the deploy, or one whose password was changed once after the deploy, change its password through UNOS, then scripts/dev/sd.sh measure around a sign-in with the password just replaced shows about 0 MiB and passdb.tdb's mtime unchanged, and a sign-in with a wrong password that the account never had leaves it as well while no lockout counts failures (ADR-0310); the same after a reboot. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): ADR-0278 and the device check above now say that a password enters the history only when it is set while the policy is 3, and ADR-0281 lists the whole [global] with the lines of step 1, superseding ADR-0087. Device check 2026-11-08: smb.conf has log file = /run/samba/log.samba, max log size = 100, log level = 1 auth_audit:2 and logging = syslog@2, and testparm accepts it. Device evidence of 2026-11-09: the smb area of scripts/dev/scenario.sh all, with the runtime files of main 12483dd, at 07:43 UTC and, after the reboot of 12:22 UTC, at 13:58 UTC passed its steps 3 (Samba runs UNOS's smb.conf with a password history of 3), 19 (the replaced password refused, passdb.tdb's time of change as before) and 23 (log file = /run/samba/log.samba, max log size = 100, and /var/log/samba's logs did not grow); its step 21 (a password the account never had, refused; 0.000 MiB at 13:58 UTC) did not look at passdb.tdb then. Measured at 14:24 UTC, after that reboot only (ADR-0310): with bad lockout attempt 0 and password history 3, four sign-ins with passwords a temporary account never had and one with its replaced password each left passdb.tdb's modification time as it was, at 0.000 to 0.016 MiB each; the account was deleted again (1.496 MiB for the whole measurement). GET /audit/logs with the search "password history" answered one entry, "SMB startup reconcile: Set Samba's password history to 3 (it was 0)" of 2026-11-08 04:02 UTC: every start since read the policy without setting it. Since 2026-11-09 the smb check's step with a wrong password compares passdb.tdb's modification time, and its step 3 expects bad lockout attempt 0 (a fresh-context review had found that the step compared nothing). That check passed on 2026-11-09 with the runtime files of main 31ac73b, in scripts/dev/scenario.sh all from 18:25:55 UTC and, after the reboot of 18:41 UTC, from 18:43:12 UTC: its step 3 read no lockout and a password history of 3, and its steps 19 (the replaced password) and 21 (a password the account never had) each left passdb.tdb's time of change as it was, at 0.016 and 0.000 MiB both times. Not checked on the device, and no longer asked for: setting a previous password again through UNOS, which smbpasswd as root does without the history's check (ADR-0278); neither the entry's steps nor the smb check, reviewed on 2026-11-09, name it.

features.description: Repeated failed SMB sign-ins are slowed down or locked out, and SMB-bound passwords on a list of common passwords are refused
steps: After repeated failed SMB sign-ins, further attempts from that client or for that account are refused for a while (a rate limit or a lockout)
