features.notes: Step 2 built (ADR-0279): constants.smb_password_problem refuses a password whose casefolded form is a line of supervisor/src/shares/common_passwords.txt (about 1450 passwords compiled for UNOS, each of at least 8 characters) with "SMB passwords must not be common passwords: this one is on the list of passwords that attackers try first", after the rules of length, size and control characters, wherever SMB-bound passwords are checked. UNOS checks only the passwords that it gives to Samba: Samba's own password change (SAMR) still takes a common password without UNOS, until shares.password-changes-only-through-unos refuses such changes (ADR-0250), so step 2 holds for the changes made through UNOS; and an account that got its password before the list keeps it until its next change. The password that goes back to Samba when the user's own password change fails after smbpasswd ran (ADR-0124) is checked without the list, so that such an account keeps SMB (test_smb_accounts.py TestCommitFailureAfterSmbpasswd and TestSmbpasswdTimeout, test_smb_models.py). Tests: test_smb_models.py (the rule in any case, the order of the rules, the format of the list), test_smb_accounts.py TestCommonPasswords (creating a user with SMB creates nothing; an administrator's and the user's own activation; the password change of an active account by the user and by an administrator; users without SMB keep any password; the text of the E2E fake), users.spec.ts 'creating a user with SMB and a common password is refused with the reason, and creates nobody' (stand-in, the real server) and 'a common password is refused for SMB, and the dialog shows why' (route fakes), account-smb.spec.ts 'turning SMB on with it is refused with the reason and how to go on' (stand-in, the real server) and 'with SMB on, a common password is refused with the reason and nothing changes' (route fakes: the stand-in has no Samba, so no account is active there). Step 2 changes nothing on the host. Reviewed in a fresh context (ADR-0017): a failed change away from a common password that an account got before the list now puts it back instead of turning SMB off, and ADR-0279 names the two exceptions above. Step 1 not built: how to limit repeated failed sign-ins is a security trade-off for the owner (ADR-0280): Samba's lockout policy per account (pdbedit -P "bad lockout attempt", "lockout duration" and "reset count minutes", set by the reconcile like the password history of ADR-0278; any client on the LAN could keep an account locked), a limit per client for TCP port 445 in a host firewall that UNOS would manage, or blocking a client that keeps failing, found in the auth_audit lines of shares.smb-auth-audit-logging. Until then unthrottled SMB sign-ins stay an accepted risk (ADR-0280); the chosen limit needs its host change and a device check.

features.description: Failed SMB sign-ins are logged with the client and the account, so that a client that keeps failing can be found
steps: A failed SMB sign-in is logged through Samba's auth_audit class, with the client's address and the account name
An administrator finds these lines in System > Logs and sees which client keeps failing
features.notes: Built (ADR-0277). Step 1: the rendered [global] has `log level = 1 auth_audit:2`, `logging = syslog@2` and `debug timestamp = no`: Samba logs a failed sign-in in its class auth_audit at level 2 and a successful one at 3, the syslog backend takes level 2, and the other classes stay at level 1 (test_smbconf.py TestGlobal); deploy/install.sh writes the same (test_deploy_scripts.py), and ADR-0281 lists the whole [global] with these lines, superseding ADR-0087. Step 2: the source Samba of System > Logs (smbd.service, nmbd.service) lists these lines newest first as notices, and its search finds them by `Auth:` or by a client's address (test_logs_sources.py TestFailedSmbSignIns, against the fake journal; logs.spec.ts 'failed SMB sign-ins: Samba lists them, and a search shows the client that keeps failing', with route fakes: the stand-in has no journal); docs/USER_GUIDE.md (Logs) says how. Device check (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): test_smbconf_testparm.py passes against the device's testparm; after the deploy's apply reloaded Samba, a sign-in with a wrong password (for example smbclient on the device against 127.0.0.1 as the account test) adds one journal entry of smbd.service with priority notice that starts with `Auth:` and holds `status [NT_STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD]`, the account and `remote host [ipv4:127.0.0.1:`; a successful sign-in adds none; GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=Auth: lists the entry and System > Logs shows it; Samba's other messages come without their header line; the same after a reboot. Device check 2026-11-08: a failed SMB sign-in (smbclient with an account that does not exist) was logged by auth_audit with the account, the status and the client's address, and GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=<account> found it. `test_smbconf_testparm.py` against the device's testparm (Samba 4.22.6), 2026-11-08: its logging test expected a `log level` line and `debug timestamp = no`; the dump of `testparm -s` shows no `log level` line, not even for a debug class that Samba lacks, and names `debug timestamp` `timestamp logs`, so of `log level` testparm checks only the parameter's name, never its classes or levels. The test now asserts `timestamp logs = no` beside the log file, its size limit and the syslog level, and all 11 tests pass there (0 MiB); the level of auth_audit rests on test_smbconf.py. Re-check after the reboot of 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, main 78769b4, the boot of 22:59:48 UTC), from the journal of the smb scenario check's run at 23:03 UTC: its account's two wrong passwords each added one entry of smbd.service with priority notice that starts with `Auth:` and holds `status [NT_STATUS_WRONG_PASSWORD]`, the account and `remote host [ipv4:127.0.0.1:`; its successful sign-ins added none, so auth_audit logs at level 2, not 3; no smbd message of that run has a header line; and GET /api/v1/logs/entries?source=samba&search=<account> lists both entries.

The logs of a container stream live over the WebSocket

features.description: An app can be installed to run in the SMB group, so that it can use a share's folder
steps: Install offers to run the app in the SMB group, which sets its PGID to 70000 (unos-smb)

features.notes: Built (ADR-0274): the install option run_in_unos_smb, the checkbox "Run in the group unos-smb" of the app's details, exists for the apps of linuxserver.io images with a pool folder outside {pool}/apps (can_run_in_unos_smb) and adds PUID 80000 (SMB_APP_UID, no other app's user), PGID 70000 and UMASK 007 to the container's environment; other images ignore PUID and PGID, and the option is refused for them and for apps with only their own data. features.description: An administrator creates a configuration backup, encrypted with a passphrase if wanted, and downloads it

With a passphrase the backup is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and named .tar.gz.enc
Download saves the file with the session, and a download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page
A backup that cannot be created, deleted or downloaded is reported on the page

Upload an encrypted .tar.gz.enc backup: it is stored as uploaded_<date>_<time>.tar.gz.enc and checked when it is restored
A plain backup named .tar.gz.enc, a corrupt archive and a file over 256 MiB are refused and leave nothing behind

An encrypted backup restores with its passphrase and is refused without it

A second restore while one runs is refused

steps: A backup task encrypts what it stores with AES-256-GCM and a passphrase, as a manual backup with a passphrase is (.tar.gz.enc)

A download with an expired session leads to the sign-in page

Select items, choose Copy or Move, open the destination and choose Copy here or Move here
An item whose name exists at the destination is neither copied nor moved
Delete removes the selected items

A name that exists or breaks the name rules is refused

features.description: Folders made with New Folder and files uploaded in Files inside a share are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Create a folder and upload a file in a share's folder in Files: they get the group unos-smb with group write (2770 for the folder, 0660 for the file)
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the file and creates entries in the folder at once
Outside share folders the File Manager creates entries as before
features.notes: Built (ADR-0273): New Folder and Upload give the new entry 2770 or 0660 when the folder it is made in is setgid, of the group unos-smb with group rwx and nothing for others (_share_folder in supervisor/src/files/router.py); the group comes from the folder, and elsewhere new entries keep what the umask leaves. A new folder that cannot get 2770 is removed again, or the answer says that it stays private, since Repair permissions skips private folders. Copy and Move keep the modes of the items, also into a share (files.group-writable-copies-and-moves-in-shares). Steps 1 and 3 are asserted by test_files_security.py, test_upload_streaming.py and test_share_api.py (TestFileManagerInAShareFolder) with the runner's gid as the SMB group, and step 3 in the web UI by files.spec.ts ('outside share folders, a new folder and an upload give the group no write access'); the stand-in cannot give a folder gid 70000. The device check, and again after a reboot (ADR-0018): in the folder of a share that UNOS created (2770 root:unos-smb) and that gives an active SMB user Read & write, create a folder and upload a file in Files: stat -c '%a %U:%G' shows 2770 root:unos-smb and 660 root:unos-smb. That user then, over SMB (smbclient), overwrites the file and puts a file into the new folder, without a Repair. A folder and an upload made in Files in a pool's top folder, which is never a share's folder, show 755 and 644 root:root (a volume that is shared and was repaired is a share folder: there they get 2770 and 660). Device check 2026-11-08: New Folder in /mnt/pools/data/shared made the folder 2770 with the group unos-smb. The rest is the scenario checks' (the feature-pass skill's table): scripts/dev/scenario.sh smb (step 10: New Folder and Upload in a new share's folder give 2770 and 660 root:unos-smb; step 11: over SMB the share's user changes the uploaded file and puts a file into the new folder) and files (steps 3 and 4: 755 and 644 root:root outside share folders) passed with the runtime files of main 12483dd at 07:43 UTC on 2026-11-09 and, after the reboot of 12:22 UTC, at 13:58 UTC (ADR-0018), as with main 78769b4 on 2026-11-08 before and after its reboot (22:33 and 23:03 UTC).

features.description: Items that Copy, or Move from another pool or volume, put into a share in Files are writable for the share's SMB users without a Repair
steps: Copy a file and a folder into a share's folder in Files: the copies get the group unos-smb with group write (folders 2770, files 0660, or 0770 for files their owner may run, as Repair permissions gives them)
Move a file and a folder from another pool or volume into a share's folder: they get the same modes
An SMB user with write access to the share changes the copied and moved items at once
Outside share folders Copy and Move keep the modes of the items, as before
features.notes: Copies keep the modes of their source (_copy_entry in supervisor/src/files/router.py), and so do moves to another pool or volume, which copy: such items need Repair permissions (ADR-0155), while New Folder and Upload give share modes (ADR-0273, files.group-writable-entries-in-shares). A Move within a pool or volume is a rename and keeps the modes as well; whether it should change them is open.

features.description: Items deleted in the file manager can be brought back for a while
steps: Delete items in Files: they go to the trash of their pool or volume, and their folder no longer lists them
On the Trash page, restore deleted items: they are back where they were, and a name that is taken there again is refused
They are gone for good only after a set time, 30 days after their deletion, or when an administrator empties the trash or deletes them from it
features.notes: Built 2026-11-07 (ADR-0259, which filled in the steps for the trash it chose; step 3 keeps the original guarantee: the Delete dialog offers no Delete for good before the server refused the move): Delete in Files moves items into <pool>/.unos-trash or <pool>/<volume>/.unos-trash with one rename, a private folder (mode 0700) per item with the item and its origin; a trash that someone else made first is made the supervisor's with mode 0700 before it is used, one that cannot be made so is refused (409), and only private folders in a trash count as its entries; every item is checked before any is moved (also bind mounts on the way, from the mount table), and one that fails after others went answers with how many went; the Delete dialog offers Delete for good (?permanent=true) only after a 409 or 507 refusal of the move, and after any refusal it holds only the items still in their folder, with the focus on Cancel; GET /files/trash, POST /files/trash/restore (every item checked first, also that its folder is on the filesystem of its pool or volume and below no mount point), DELETE /files/trash and POST /files/trash/empty; trash_expiry_loop in the lifespan, at the start and once a day; the name .unos-trash is hidden, refused and left out of copies, every share section vetoes it and it cannot be shared; on the Trash page each checkbox is labelled with the item's name, folder and deletion time. Asserted on this machine: step 1 by test_files_security.py (the trash tests, volumes and deeper subvolumes through st_dev fakes, trashes of other owners through fakes of st_uid, bind mounts through the mount table fake) and files.spec.ts ('deletes the selected items', 'Delete offers no Delete for good until the trash has refused the items', the keyboard test and the two refusal tests of the Delete dialog); step 2 by the test_restore_ and test_a_restore_ tests and files.spec.ts ('the Trash page lists deleted items, and Restore puts them back where they were', 'a restore is refused while the name is taken again, and the item stays in the trash', 'the Trash page tells items of the same name apart by where and when they were deleted'); step 3 by test_deleted_items_are_deleted_for_good_30_days_after_their_deletion, test_an_administrator_deletes_items_for_good_or_empties_the_trash, test_a_trash_that_others_can_change_is_made_private_and_what_they_put_there_is_no_entry, the expiry loop tests, test_lifespan.py and files.spec.ts ('the Trash page deletes items for good, and Empty trash deletes everything', 'Delete offers no Delete for good until the trash has refused the items'). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step: every share section of the rendered smb.conf has veto files = /.snapshots/.unos-trash/ and testparm takes it; a file and a folder deleted in /mnt/pools/data/shared land in /mnt/pools/data/.unos-trash (mode 0700) and Restore brings them back; a file deleted in a volume lands in that volume's .unos-trash through the real btrfs rename, not in the pool's, and comes back; a .unos-trash that a user other than root made in a volume with mode 0777 is root's with mode 0700 after the next listing (the real fchown, which the tests fake); a file in a snapshot or in the restored copy of a volume's snapshot answers 409 (no trash) and, after that refusal, Delete for good removes the latter; smbclient lists no .unos-trash in the share of a volume; a delete, a restore and an expiry pass write 0 MiB to the SD card; after a reboot the items are still listed, and an entry renamed to a time 31 days back is gone after the pass at the start. The backend tests ran on macOS (renameatx_np, and APFS takes only UTF-8 names): scripts/dev/linux-tests.sh tests/test_files_security.py runs them with renameat2 across two folders and restores a name that is not UTF-8. roles.spec.ts keeps regular users off the Trash page. Whether the Delete dialog should offer Delete for good before a refusal is the owner's decision (ADR-0259, Considered options). Device check 2026-11-08 after the deploy: a file deleted on the pool data and in the share's folder went into /mnt/pools/data/.unos-trash (mode 700, root), came back with Restore, and went for good from the trash; every share of smb.conf has the trash's veto line and testparm accepts it. Open: a volume's own trash, the 409 of a snapshot, the listing after a reboot and the 30-day expiry.

features.description: The dashboard shows live CPU, memory, network and disk I/O over the WebSocket, and the storage overview
steps: Open the dashboard: the stats arrive over the WebSocket, and the CPU, memory and network values change with them, without HTTP polling
The storage widget shows the pools with the health the API reports

features.description: System > Resource Monitor shows CPU, memory, network and disk I/O with their history, and the process list
steps: Open System > Resource Monitor: CPU, memory, network throughput and disk I/O are shown
The time range buttons change the history shown
The process list shows the running processes with their CPU and memory use
features.notes: The E2E spec checks the tab's headings only, and no backend test covers the monitor API.

features.description: The dashboard shows the host's CPU temperature, and the API lists every sensor
steps: The dashboard's CPU card shows the temperature of the host's CPU
GET /api/v1/system/temperatures lists each sensor group with its readings
A host without sensors shows that none are available

features.description: System > Network shows the host's interfaces, DNS, gateway, routes and connections, and an administrator brings an interface up or down
steps: Open System > Network: each interface is listed with its addresses, state and speed
DNS servers, search domains, the gateway and the routing table are shown
Bring an interface down and up again: its state follows on the host
features.notes: Built (ADR-0245): every command of the network API runs on the host through src/host.py. GET /network/interfaces lists each interface's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, its operational state, whether it is enabled, and its link speed from the host's sysfs; VLANs (eth0.100) are listed and changed like the others; the routes are the IPv4 and IPv6 tables; DNS reads all of resolvectl's servers and leaves out its fallback servers; a failed request answers 500 with the host's message (a host that does not answer in time: "the host did not answer within N seconds"), and the page shows it. The tab is built from the UI components and tokens. Disable and Enable follow ADR-0244 (system.network-disable-confirmation). The fake-host tests and the E2E spec (route fakes: the stand-in has no host network) pass. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214): System > Network on the dev device lists its NICs and the Hurricane Electric tunnel with the addresses, states and speeds that `ip addr` and `cat /sys/class/net/<if>/speed` show on the host, and the DNS servers, search domains, gateway and routes of `resolvectl status`, `ip route` and `ip -6 route`; Disable and Enable of a NIC that does not carry the connection, and carries no VLANs (ADR-0246), follow on the host (`ip link`). The live rates on the page still come from the supervisor container's interfaces, matched by name (system.dashboard). PUT /network/hostname duplicates PUT /system/hostname (system.hostname-and-time-zone), and GET /system/network, which no page calls, duplicates GET /network/interfaces with ethtool speeds. Device check 2026-11-07: GET /api/v1/network/interfaces showed enP4p65s0 at 2500 Mb/s with its IPv4 and IPv6 addresses; DNS (10.1.1.1), the gateway and the routes were shown; the VLAN enP4p65s0.99, added for the check and removed after it, went down and up again on the host through the API.

features.description: An administrator sets the host's name and time zone
steps: Set the hostname in System > General: hostnamectl on the host shows it
Set the time zone: timedatectl on the host shows it, and scheduled tasks follow it
features.notes: The commands run inside the supervisor container (architecture.host-command-layer). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018).

features.description: An administrator reboots, shuts down or suspends the host, cancels a pending shutdown, and turns Wake-on-LAN on
steps: Reboot and Shutdown in System > Power ask for confirmation, then act on the host one minute later
Cancel stops a pending reboot or shutdown
Turn Wake-on-LAN on for an interface: ethtool on the host shows it, and the Power tab says that a magic packet starts a host that is off only where the board keeps the network card powered
features.notes: Built (ADR-0233): reboot, shutdown, cancel, suspend and Wake-on-LAN run on the host through src/host.py; GET /api/v1/power/pending reads logind's ScheduledShutdown, and Cancel runs shutdown -c only while something is pending; the Wake-on-LAN choice per interface is kept in /data/wol_config.json and set again at each start of the supervisor; with UNOS_HOST_EXEC=local (the stand-in, the test stack) every power endpoint answers 503 and runs nothing; POST /system/reboot, /system/shutdown and /system/cancel-shutdown are gone. System > Power shows each answer, the pending action with its Cancel button, and the interfaces with their MAC address and an on or off button; Suspend asks first too. Proven on a fake host and with route fakes only: every step acts on the host, so the entry passes after the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), and reboots of the dev device are owner actions (ADR-0211). The device check must show: Reboot in the tab makes busctl get-property org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager ScheduledShutdown name reboot one minute ahead, and the host reboots then; Cancel empties it and nothing happens; Shutdown powers the host off a minute later; Turn on for the board's NIC makes ethtool <nic> on the host show Wake-on: g, a magic packet from a second machine on the LAN starts the host after a shutdown (whether the NIC and the board support it is unknown), and after a reboot ethtool still shows g. The host needs ethtool; the startup check names it when it is missing. The UPS monitor still shuts down only outside a container (system.ups-monitoring). Device check 2026-11-07: Wake-on-LAN on and off through the API showed Wake-on: g and d in ethtool on the host; a reboot was pending one minute later and Cancel stopped it; a reboot from the API rebooted the host (back after 114 s, with the pool mounted, Samba, the share and the containers up). Magic packets from the workstation did not start the dev device after a shutdown: its board cuts the network card's power (ADR-0247).

features.description: With NUT configured, System > Power shows the UPS state, and UNOS shuts the host down on low battery
steps: Configure the UPS: the battery charge, the runtime and the state are shown
On battery below the set level, UNOS sends an alert and shuts the host down
Test connection names a failure
features.notes: The monitor starts in the lifespan, but nothing tests it. Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018). In the supervisor container the monitor never shuts the host down (step 2): it starts the shutdown only when is_in_container() is false, and /.dockerenv makes it true (supervisor/src/power/router.py).

features.description: The host shuts down, and wakes, at the times set in the power settings
steps: Set an auto-shutdown time: the host shuts down then
Set a wake time: the host wakes then (rtcwake)
Idle shutdown turns the host off after the idle time
features.notes: PUT /api/v1/power/config stores these settings, but nothing acts on them, and no page shows them.

features.description: System > Logs shows the host's journal, kernel messages and log files, with filters and search
steps: Pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first
Search highlights matches and shows markup in log lines as text
The filters are comboboxes named by their labels
features.notes: Built (ADR-0257, ADR-0258): every source is a part of the host's journal, read with one journalctl command on the host through src/host.py, newest first (--reverse --lines=<limit>), off the event loop: System Journal (all of it), Kernel (--dmesg), Docker (docker.service), Samba (smbd.service, nmbd.service), Authentication (the syslog facilities auth and authpriv) and Cron Jobs (cron.service); UNOS Supervisor and Web Server are no longer sources. journalctl runs under the host's timeout(1) (`timeout --kill-after=5 30`), which ends it on the host after 30 seconds, and at most two reads run at once, on a pool of threads of their own. In every source a severity lists that level and the more severe ones and the time range applies, and the search is journalctl's literal, case-insensitive --grep, so it finds the newest matches of the whole range; a search without a match (status 1 without output) lists no entries. The output is split at \n alone, so an entry with U+2028 stays one entry. The tab shows the entries in the answer's order, says newest first, shows the times in the browser's time zone, sends a new limit with its request, shows only the answer of its newest request, shows an error instead of the list, and Auto and Search wait for an answer that is still coming. Step 1: tests/test_logs_sources.py (TestSources: each source's command and its entries, newest first; TestSeverity: every level in every source; TestTimeRange; TestEntries, with U+2028, the host's timeout and two reads at a time off the default executor; TestErrors, with a journalctl that reads too long ended on the host; TestValues, TestRoles, TestLegacyRoutes) and logs.spec.ts 'pick a source and a severity: the entries are listed, newest first', 'the limit and the time range reach the server with the request they change', 'Auto asks again every 5 seconds, but not while an answer is still coming', 'a late answer for the source picked before does not replace the entries of the one picked last' and 'an error of the server is shown instead of the entries of the request before'. Step 2: logs.spec.ts 'search highlighting shows markup in log lines as text', 'a search asks the server: the matches it lists are highlighted, and no match says so' and 'Search waits while an answer is still coming', and TestSearch (with a search that finds nothing) and TestEntries for the server. POST /network/interfaces/{name}/down saves the interface's addresses and routes in /run/unos/network on the host, arms the transient systemd timer unos-network-revert-<if> (60 seconds) and only then disables it; it refuses (the interface stays enabled) when the state cannot be saved or the timer cannot be armed, and (409) for an interface that carries VLANs without loose binding, which the kernel turns off and on with it. Without Keep the timer turns the interface back on with its saved addresses and routes, also when the supervisor restarts. When the page's time runs out it looks again 5 seconds later and reports what it finds: back on, still counting on the host (countdown and Keep again), still off with nothing waiting (a revert that could not turn it on, or a Keep elsewhere: reported, with Enable), gone from the host, or not readable. Wherever UNOS finds the interface on again (Enable, Keep), it discards the saved state, unless the revert is restoring it. The fake-host tests, the tests of the host scripts under sh and dash and the E2E spec pass. Built: the lookup and the stores of webui/src/lib/i18n/ (one catalog per area with English and Russian halves, plural forms by Intl.PluralRules, the choice kept in this browser as unos-locale, <html lang> after it, Russian by default for a browser set to Russian, dates in the browser's format when it is of the page's language and else day first on a 24-hour clock), the Language card of the Account page, and the texts in both languages of the navigation and the frame (+layout.svelte, the tabs of the System page), the login and setup pages, the Account page (SecurityTab.svelte with RecoveryCodes and SmbAccessCard; the firewall's and the certificates' values through maps from the server's values to keys, a certificate's openssl dates in the page's language) and the shared components of src/lib/components/ui. Step 1: webui/tests/language.spec.ts switches an administrator's Account page to Russian and sees the navigation and the page change at once, stay Russian after a reload and on the login page after signing out, and go back to English; switches a regular user's Account page to Russian, also after a reload; shows the firewall's and the certificates' values in both languages; and checks that a browser set to Russian starts in Russian and that an English page in it writes dates day first. It cannot see a text that the code puts together from data at run time, a single lower-case word in a script, or a .ts module, so the empty list is necessary, not sufficient: passes stays false until the list is empty and a walk through every page in Russian, by a reviewer in a fresh context, finds no English text other than the server's messages. The names, descriptions and variables of the apps and their memory recommendations stay in English, as the server's app catalog has them, so the walk of ADR-0287 still finds English there. ADR-0291, proposed to the owner and not yet decided, would count them with the server's messages and keep the category list's labels on the English cards (Smart Home, AI & LLMs and Downloads, where they said Home Automation, Ai and Download); refused, the cards get keys of their own with their former words, and the app catalog needs a translation before this feature passes. Second phase, the dashboard and Files: the dashboard (src/routes/+page.svelte and its widgets, the containers' states through a map) and Files with its trash, with the units of their sizes, rates and times from their own catalogs and the numbers' decimal point kept (ADR-0297); dashboard.spec.ts ('shows the dashboard in Russian', with the stats cards of a fake stats socket, and a regular user's) and files.spec.ts ('shows Files and the trash in Russian', 'Files and the trash count, size and date their items in Russian') show them in Russian, with the counts in their plural forms, the sizes, rates, times and dates that the code puts together at run time, while the server's messages stay English; dashboard.spec.ts 'the stats cards write sizes, rates and the temperature with their units' keeps their English. The check of the texts does not see either, so the walk of ADR-0287 has to. Translated in phase B: System > Notifications and System > Network (NotificationsTab.svelte and NetworkTab.svelte, catalogs notifications and network), off the list; webui/tests/notifications.spec.ts and webui/tests/network.spec.ts check each tab in Russian (its texts, plural forms, the server's values through maps of keys, a channel's events by their names, dates, and the link speeds and the live traffic of the stats stream in the page's units and number format), and the values that ip and ss print in the Network tab's tables stay as they come (ADR-0295); supervisor/tests/test_notifications.py checks that the English half of the notifications catalog names and describes the server's events word for word. formatBytes and formatBytesPerSecond of webui/src/lib/stores/stats.ts still write English units on the pages that use them. Second phase, the System tabs Resource Monitor, System Logs, Disk Health and Power Management and the Audit Log page: they take their texts from the catalogs monitor, logs, health, power and audit, and the server's values through maps (log sources, levels and time ranges; SMART states, attribute states, NVMe fields and the units of a disk's capacity; audit actions, severities and types of resource). Each spec of these pages has a test in Russian, and test_logs_sources.py, test_audit_log.py and test_health_smart.py tie the maps to the server's log sources, audit actions and types of resource, and disk capacities. On a Russian page the Audit Log names actions and resources in Russian, but its search finds them by their English words only, as the page says when a search finds nothing, while ADR-0237 has the search find them as the page shows them: ADR-0298, proposed to the owner and not yet decided, would make that exception, and until then ADR-0237 stands and this feature does not pass with it; refused, the Russian page names them by ADR-0237's English words, or the search also finds the names of the page's language. Step 1: TestRunbook in tests/test_emergency.py checks that every mount of the runbook is read-only without the log replay (rescue=nologreplay; noload for the old system disk's ext4), that the desktop's automounting is turned off before a disk is attached and lsblk -f shows the pool's disks, and the old system disk, unmounted before their read-only mounts, that one mounts degraded, that no command writes to a pool, that its table of the disks each profile may miss covers PROFILE_MAP, that the places it names (.snapshots, the snap_, auto_ and restore_ names, .unos-trash, /mnt/pools, apps, smb.conf and the table smb_shares in the volume deploy_unos-data, the group 70000, the SMB user ids from 70000 and mode 2770) and the reset command with its rules are those of the code's constants, and that it says what to do when someone else may know the old password: a new JWT secret, the account's API tokens, the accounts it created, changed or made administrators (the Users page and the user entries of the audit log), and what the audit log does not record yet. Step 2: TestReset, TestPassword and TestSafety run the command against the temporary database and audit log of test_smb_accounts.World: the new password signs in through the API without a code and the old one gets 401; 2FA, its secret and the recovery codes are gone; the audit log, also through GET /api/v1/audit/logs, has password_change and, when 2FA was on, totp_disabled, by the user root for the resource user NAME, severity warning; the password comes from standard input or twice from a terminal, never from argv, and is in no output, log or audit entry; at least 8 characters, at most 72 bytes, no control characters; without NAME the only administrator, several administrators or a NAME that is not an administrator change nothing; a missing database is not created; an administrator changed while the password is typed (2FA turned on, demoted, its id given to another user or to another administrator) is not reset; an audit entry that cannot be written is reported with exit status 1; names from a restored database reach the terminal without control characters; no module of supervisor/src imports the command and no route reaches it. TestResetAdminScript runs deploy/reset-admin.sh with a fake docker that starts the module in a process of its own: docker exec -i unos-supervisor python -m src.emergency reset-admin [NAME], -it on a terminal, the password only on standard input, refused without root; the container name, WORKDIR /app and COPY src/ match the compose file and the Dockerfile. TestBesideTheSupervisor: the command's audit entries wait for a rotation in the supervisor's process and none is lost, as the log's lock holds across processes (ADR-0286; TestOtherProcesses in tests/test_audit_log.py). webui/tests/emergency-reset.spec.ts, on the local stand-in: an administrator with 2FA stops at the code step, scripts/standin/emergency.py resets it against the stand-in's data beside its running supervisor, the browser signs in with the new password without a code, the old one gets 401, and the Audit Log page shows Totp disabled and Password change by root for user NAME (TestStandInCommand checks the script). Device check, still open: (1) on a Linux machine with btrfs-progs and Linux 5.9 or later, with the disks of a two-disk raid1 pool that UNOS made (or loop-device images on the Linux test runner), the commands of docs/RECOVERY.md find it by its label, mount it with -o ro,rescue=nologreplay, list its volumes, .snapshots and share folders as the runbook says, copy a file with rsync, and mount it again with -o ro,degraded,rescue=nologreplay with one disk detached, while the write counters of the disks (/sys/block/<disk>/stat) stay unchanged; and on a desktop live session (Ubuntu's GNOME), with automounting turned off as the runbook says, attaching the disks mounts none of them (lsblk -f) and their write counters stay unchanged from the attach on; (2) on the dev device, an owner action because it changes credentials (ADR-0024): for a throwaway administrator with 2FA, sudo /opt/unos/deploy/reset-admin.sh <name> asks for the password twice on a terminal and also takes it on standard input, the name then signs in at the web UI with the new password without a code, the Audit Log page shows password_change and totp_disabled by root, and scripts/dev/sd.sh measure gives the SD writes of a reset. features.notes: Built 2026-11-08 (ADR-0283, which superseded ADR-0282 after the fresh-context review). The pool of a name is the btrfs filesystem labelled with it, or of several with one label, the one mounted or managed under it: GET /api/v1/storage/pools lists those, and Mount imports a pool found on the disks (its dialog says the disks are not formatted). Any other btrfs filesystem that is neither the host's system filesystem nor mounted is listed by GET /api/v1/storage/filesystems/importable and under Found on the disks; POST /api/v1/storage/filesystems/{uuid}/import mounts it by UUID at /mnt/pools/<name>, checks that the mount shows the top level, sets the name as its label through the mount, has udev read its devices again and writes the managed fstab entry. Filesystems on boot or virtual devices (the SD card, the eMMC, loop and RAM disks) or on the system disk are neither offered nor listed, and Mount and Import refuse them; an import under a name that SMB shares, NFS exports or containers of an earlier pool still use is refused. A refused or failed import leaves no mountpoint, fstab line or label behind, and Mount, Import and Create undo a mount that shows another subvolume than the top level. Asserted on fakes: step 1 by test_pool_import.py (what is offered: labels, duplicates, boot, virtual and system devices) and storage.spec.ts (Pool import: the offer, the dialog, the refusals, two filesystems with one label, Mount of a found pool); step 2 by test_pool_import.py (the fstab entry by UUID, the mount from it after a reboot, the used bytes kept, no mkfs, the refusals and what an undo leaves), test_pool_persistence.py (TestMountPool) and test_smb_integration.py (an import under the name of a removed pool serves none of its shares). Open: the device check and the re-check after a reboot (ADR-0018), with the SD MiB of each step (ADR-0214); it needs a spare disk, which the dev device does not have. On it: (1) read only, first: GET /api/v1/storage/pools and GET /api/v1/storage/filesystems/importable list nothing on mmcblk0 (the eMMC) or mmcblk1 (the SD card); nothing is ever imported or mounted there (ADR-0225). (2) A btrfs filesystem without a label (mkfs.btrfs without -L) that holds a few files, not mounted: Storage lists it under Found on the disks with its UUID and size; Import as importtest mounts it at /mnt/pools/importtest by UUID (findmnt), /etc/fstab holds the marker and the UUID entry, btrfs filesystem show and lsblk show the label importtest, and the files are there; after a reboot it is mounted again with its files. (3) An SMB share on importtest, then Remove Pool: the files stay on the disk. Clear the label while it is unmounted (btrfs filesystem label <device> ''): Import as importtest answers 409 and names the share, and nothing changes; after the share is deleted, the import succeeds. (4) Remove Pool, then label the filesystem with a pool name: it is listed as Not mounted, and Mount imports it. (5) Remove Pool, clear the label, mount it by hand, run btrfs subvolume set-default with another subvolume and unmount it: Import as importtest answers 409 with the subvolume message, findmnt shows nothing at /mnt/pools/importtest, that directory does not exist, btrfs filesystem show prints no label, and /etc/fstab is unchanged; labelled with a pool name, Mount answers 409, it stays unmounted and /etc/fstab is unchanged.
